svg.title: Stopping & momentum
svg.desc: Thinking & braking: Stopping distance = thinking + braking. Thinking = speed × reaction time. Typical reaction time 0.2–0.9 s. Tiredness, drugs/alcohol and distractions can delay reaction. Ruler-drop tests: repeat, control setup, consider anticipation. Braking factors: Wet/icy roads, worn tyres/brakes reduce effective braking. Friction transfers kinetic energy to thermal stores. Same mass/force: double speed → four times braking distance. Thinking only doubles at fixed reaction time. Large deceleration risks overheating/loss of control. Momentum is a vector: p = mv, kg m/s. Choose a positive direction and use signed velocities. Closed system with zero resultant external force: total momentum before = after. Collisions & recoil: 2 kg at 3 m/s joins stationary 1 kg: 6 kg m/s / 3 kg = 2 m/s. Recoil from rest: equal opposite momenta, lighter mass moves faster. Kinetic energy need not be conserved. Force changes momentum: F = Δp/Δt = m(v−u)/Δt. Gives average force for the interval. 60 kg at 10 m/s → rest: |Δp|=600 kg m/s. Over 0.20 s → 3,000 N; over 0.50 s → 1,200 N. Safety features: Airbags, belts, helmets, mats and soft surfaces increase stopping time for the same momentum change. Average force is lower. They do not stop momentum changing or destroy energy.
